## What it is

Excalidraw is a whiteboard in the browser for quick sketches and diagrams that look hand-drawn ([excalidraw/excalidraw](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw)).

**Licence:** `MIT` (GitHub licence API). Market class **L1**. There is no license-matrix row yet, so the gate notes that it is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10).

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## Market listing

- Category and sub-tags (docs/design/TAXONOMY.md §1): notes: whiteboard. The sub-tags go into `metadata.tags` once the schema has it.
- Deployment class (TAXONOMY §2): **Market · community** until CI writes a passing scan (contract §9.4), then Market · verified if every check passes. It cannot reach verified while the image is unversioned (below).

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: nginx serving the built web app. No server-side data: drawings stay in your browser's storage unless you save them to a file.
- nginx runs as its unprivileged user (UID 101) with a **read-only root filesystem** and small scratch volumes; the namespaced sysctl `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=0` lets it bind port 80 in this pod only. No privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped.
- No volume.
- Probes: `GET /` (the image's own health check).
- **Image version (UNVERIFIED):** upstream's Docker workflow pushes only `:latest`. The pinned digest was pushed on 2026-05-06 from release-branch commit `b2b2815`; publishing has failed since then, so this build is about six months older than the code. Its nginx base may carry fixed CVEs, which the CI scan reports.

## First run

Source: [docs.excalidraw.com](https://docs.excalidraw.com).

1. Install Excalidraw from the Market and approve the action. It installs into `app-excalidraw`.
2. Forward the port and open http://localhost:8080:
   ```sh
   kubectl -n app-excalidraw port-forward svc/excalidraw 8080:8080
   ```
3. Draw. Use the menu to save a drawing to a `.excalidraw` file.

## Privacy note

The built app keeps excalidraw.com's own services for "Live collaboration" and "Shareable link": using them sends the drawing (encrypted in the browser, per upstream) to servers run by Excalidraw. Saving to a file sends nothing. A self-hosted collaboration server is not packaged.

## Not done yet

- No versioned image (above); no self-hosted collaboration or share-link backend.
- No HTTPS or LAN hostname: OneMind v0 has no ingress or certificates for apps, so the app is reached through a port-forward until the app proxy exists.
- Resource figures are OneMind choices; upstream publishes none. They are checked against real use when the CI smoke test (contract §9.4 check 9) runs.
- `metadata.tier` stays `community` until `sdk/tools/app-gate` in CI writes a passing `scan.json`. `spec.updates.automerge` is `none` until `renovate.json` lists the app.

## Why this app is blocked

The CI app gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate`, contract §9.4) computed tier **blocked** for this app on 2026-11-12 (ci-apps run 43212771377, job `gate (excalidraw)`). The gateway lists a blocked app in the Market but refuses to install it (§10.3, §11.1). The app is kept, not hidden, and the gate was not weakened. Reasons from that run:

- Vulnerability: `docker.io/excalidraw/excalidraw:latest` (pinned by digest; upstream publishes only a floating tag): CVE-2026-111497 in `brotli-libs` 1.1.0-r2 (fixed 1.1.1-r0); CVE-2026-31789 in `libcrypto3` and `libssl3` 3.3.3-r0 (fixed 3.3.7-r0).
- Licence: GitHub MIT matches, but there is no research licence-matrix row, so the app is not preinstallable on sold boxes until one is added (brief 30 B10). The app still carries `UNVERIFIED` markers (README, deployment.yaml).
- Passed: ClamAV (0 infected), smoke test (GET / returned 200).

To unblock: move the pins to upstream releases that fix these findings (tags that exist, checked with `crane`), then rerun `sdk/tools/app-gate` (the daily `apps-rescan` workflow does this too). Nothing is bumped to an unverified tag.
